verdicts.title: chore(main): release 2.3.1
verdicts.rationale: PR #199 is a routine release-please release PR. Its own diff is trivial and correct: +8/-1 across CHANGELOG.md (adds a 2.3.1 section crediting #197 signing/dropNulls + #198 OIDC CI fix) and package.json (2.3.0 -> 2.3.1). It is NOT stale: the head branch (release-please--branches--main--components--sdk, tip 41f28ba dated 2026-06-15 21:02) sits directly on top of current origin/main (dd64dea, #207), and `git log origin/main ^prbranch` is empty — release-please regenerated it after the oracle->script rename (#206) and the TS6/omnibus dep bumps (#200, #207) landed. Those chore/refactor commits are correctly omitted from the release NOTES (release-please only lists feat/fix) but ARE included in the shipped 2.3.1 artifact, so the rename is part of what publishes. mergeable=MERGEABLE, branch is up to date. HOWEVER the merge state is BLOCKED by one genuine failing required check: "Test ottochain-services" (Consumer Compatibility). Root cause is real, not flaky: ottochain-services/packages/bridge/src/metagraph.ts:9 imports `normalizeMessage` from @ottochain/sdk, but that symbol was REMOVED from the SDK public API in #197 (the same signing/dropNulls change this very release ships) — confirmed gone from local src/ (no `normalizeMessage`, no normalize export in src/index.ts). So 2.3.1 is effectively a CONSUMER-BREAKING change mis-labeled by conventional-commits as a `fix:` (patch bump). Releasing as-is publishes a patch that breaks the downstream consumer's build. This needs a human decision on semver/consumer handling, not a mechanical merge — hence needs-author-decision rather than land. The other open PRs are unrelated long-stale feature work (delegation pair #41+#95, token state machine #80 overlapping fiber-apps-overhaul, authenticated-tries/subscribeFiberState #83) and do not gate this release.
alignmentGaps: semver mislabel: #197 removed the public export `normalizeMessage` from @ottochain/sdk (gone from src/index.ts and all of src/), which is a BREAKING change for consumers, but conventional-commits classified it `fix(signing):` so release-please cut a PATCH (2.3.0 -> 2.3.1) instead of a major. Releasing 2.3.1 ships a silent API break.

Required check `Test ottochain-services` (Consumer Compatibility) FAILS: ottochain-services/packages/bridge/src/metagraph.ts(9,21) TS2305 — Module '@ottochain/sdk' has no exported member 'normalizeMessage'. This is the cause of mergeStateStatus=BLOCKED; it is a real downstream break, not a flaky/infra failure.

Release notes are scoped only to #197/#198, but the 2.3.1 artifact also ships the oracle->script API rename (#206, endpoints /data-application/v1/scripts, type ScriptInvocation) and TypeScript 6 / omnibus dep bumps (#200, #207). The rename itself is another likely consumer-breaking surface change folded into a patch release with no changelog visibility.

No coordination with downstream: the SDK removed normalizeMessage and renamed oracle->script with no corresponding update staged in /home/euler/repos/ottochain (consumer ottochain-services still on the old import).
recommendedActions: Do NOT merge #199 as-is — it would publish a consumer-breaking change as a patch. Decide semver intent first (author/human decision).

Fix the downstream consumer before/alongside release: update ottochain-services/packages/bridge/src/metagraph.ts:9 to stop importing the removed `normalizeMessage` (the SDK now applies dropNulls internally on the dataUpdate signing path per #197, so the explicit normalize call is no longer needed). Re-run the Consumer Compatibility workflow to clear the BLOCKED state.

Decide whether 2.3.1 (patch) is the correct version. Given #197 removed a public export and #206 renamed the oracle->script surface, consider re-cutting as a MINOR or MAJOR with a `feat!`/`BREAKING CHANGE:` footer so release-please labels it correctly and the changelog warns consumers.

If the consumer-compat gate is judged out-of-scope for the SDK repo's own release (the failure is in the external ottochain-services build), have a human either (a) land the consumer fix in /home/euler/repos/ottochain first, or (b) explicitly waive/override the required check — but only after the semver decision above.
Surface the rename (#206) and removal (#197) in the release notes / BREAKING_CHANGES.md so consumers migrating from 2.3.0 know normalizeMessage is gone and oracle endpoints are now /scripts.

Treat the four stale feature PRs (#41+#95 delegation, #80 token state machine vs fiber-apps-overhaul, #83 authenticated-tries/subscribeFiberState) separately; they are unrelated to this release and several are already flagged needs-manual-rebase/blocked.
risks: Merging now publishes @ottochain/sdk 2.3.1 to npm via OIDC trusted publishing (the #198/#186 pipeline is live), breaking any consumer that imports normalizeMessage — silently, since it is only a patch bump.
The oracle->script rename (#206) riding in this release can break consumers calling the old /data-application/v1/oracle endpoints or using the old type names, with no changelog warning.
Overriding the BLOCKED check without fixing the consumer leaves ottochain-services unbuildable against the published SDK.

Signing-path change (#197 dropNulls applied internally) is exactly the canonical/JCS surface where a mismatch yields opaque InvalidSignature/HTTP 400 — worth a real e2e sign+submit check against the chain before publishing, beyond just the type-level consumer test.

verdicts.title: feat: SDK delegation module — PolicyBuilder + complete API
verdicts.rationale: PR #41 implements an SDK delegation surface (DelegationClient, PolicyBuilder, generated delegation/intents protos) that was explicitly designed to pair with on-chain ottochain PR #90 "JLVM delegation operators" — which is CLOSED, never merged. The chain has no delegation concept: the JLVM var namespace in ottochain/modules/models/src/main/scala/xyz/kd5ujc/schema/fiber/ReservedKeys.scala injects $ordinal/proofs/address/expiresAt but NO `delegation.*` key, so the PolicyBuilder's core predicates (delegation.active/expiresAt/scope/relayer) reference a context object the chain never provides and would never resolve. The design has since pivoted to an asset-model symmetric-compose handshake (AuthorizeCompose, ComponentWitness, commit-reveal nonces, _transferAsset/_scriptCall), making the PR's bridge-based session-key/relayer model obsolete. On top of the semantic mismatch, the PR is mechanically unrebasable: it branches from v2.0.0 with 32 intervening commits on current (v2.3.0) including a ts-proto migration, proto unification, the normalize/drop-null rework, and the oracle→script rename; it adds a packages/ monorepo + proto/delegation that don't exist now, commits ~3,400 lines of dist/ that is now gitignored, ships ~8,300 lines of generated code from the old proto toolchain, and carries a stale 2.0.0 package.json exports map that conflicts with current and does not even export the ./delegation subpath its own README advertises. This is supersede-by-close: the feature must be redesigned against the current asset-model/script surface, not rebased.

verdicts.title: feat: add DelegationCredential proto schema + delegation messages
verdicts.rationale:
The PR adds a `DelegationCredential` record + `CreateDelegation`/`RevokeDelegation` messages and wires them into the proto schema, but the ground has moved decisively underneath it on two independent axes, and the feature has no on-chain counterpart.

(1) PROTO FIELD-NUMBER COLLISIONS — the PR was cut against an old proto. Current local /home/euler/repos/ottochain-sdk/proto/ottochain/v1/messages.proto already occupies OttochainMessage oneof fields 6-9 with upgrade_fiber=6, publish_version=7, set_version_status=8, register_alias=9 — the PR tries to add create_delegation=6 and revoke_delegation=7, a hard wire collision. Likewise proto/ottochain/v1/records.proto CalculatedState already uses field 3 (registry_entries, json_name="registry") and field 4 (reverse_names), while the PR adds delegations=3. So 'needs-manual-rebase' understates it: the PR's chosen field numbers are taken, and re-numbering changes the wire format the PR authored.

(2) NO ON-CHAIN COUNTERPART (the canonical authority). In /home/euler/repos/ottochain (Updates.scala + schema/CalculatedState.scala) there is NO delegation concept. The on-chain OttochainMessage/AssetOp set is CreateStateMachine, TransitionStateMachine, ArchiveStateMachine, UpgradeFiber, CreateScript, UpgradeScript, InvokeScript, PublishMachineVersion, PublishScriptVersion, SetVersionStatus, RegisterAlias, CreateAssetPolicy, MintAsset, ApplyMorphism, AuthorizeCompose — no Create/RevokeDelegation. On-chain CalculatedState is {stateMachines, scripts, registry, reverseNames, assets, usedNonces} — there is no `delegations` map; the chain instead grew `assets` (the PR #80 token direction) and `usedNonces`. The chain explicitly DEFERS delegation: RegistryName.scala notes 'per-label ownership/delegation arrives with the nickname-registry follow-up (#29)'. metakit has no delegation either. Because signing is JCS(dropNulls(payload)) verified on-chain (see docs/signing-and-publishing.md, guarded by PublishVersionSigningCanonicalSuite), proto types with no chain decoder are unsignable/unverifiable — any client emitting them gets InvalidSignature (opaque 400). So merging this proto ships dead, mis-numbered wire types.

(3) Stale collateral: the PR's diff still carries src/generated/ottochain/apps/oracles/v1/oracle.ts and bumps ts-proto 2.11.2->2.11.4 across all generated files; the local branch (commit 722fa8e) completed the oracle→script rename and the apps/oracles generated tree is gone, so the regen would conflict broadly and reintroduce stale 'oracles' paths.

Net: the design premise ('DelegationCredential is a first-class CalculatedState record, same tier as StateMachineFiberRecord') is contradicted by the current chain, the field numbers collide, and the regenerated TS is stale. This isn't a mechanical rebase — it's a re-design that should wait until the chain actually defines delegation (chain issue #29). Recommend close (not just block), and reopen/re-author once ottochain lands the on-chain delegation model so proto field numbers and the signing canonical can be derived from the chain rather than guessed.
dependsOn: ottochain on-chain delegation model (chain issue #29, nickname-registry follow-up) — must define DelegationCredential, CreateDelegation/RevokeDelegation, and a CalculatedState.delegations map (or equivalent) BEFORE any SDK proto can be derived
PR #41 (feat/sdk-delegation-methods — SDK delegation module / PolicyBuilder) is the API consumer of these proto types; the two are a delegation pair and share the same no-on-chain-counterpart blocker

verdicts.title: feat: Asset Model Token State Machine SDK (16 TDEG archetypes)
verdicts.rationale: The on-chain asset model (ottochain modules/models/.../asset/TokenBehavior.scala + docs/proposals/asset-model.md "RFC v2", 2026-06-15) explicitly supersedes this PR's TDEG SDK spec by name. The chain moved from a 4-bit TDEG model to a 5-bit TSCEG lattice (split Divisible into splittable+combinable; weights T=16,S=8,C=4,E=2,G=1, so every numeric value the PR asserts in its tests is now wrong: chain NFT=16 vs PR NFT=8). The chain also changed the representation entirely: behavior is a single packed Int (AssetCommit.behavior) with structure enforced via typed MorphismKinds in Scala, not a per-token StateMachineDefinition JSON with JSON-Logic guards. Additionally the PR's hand-rolled { value: string } StateId wire wrapper contradicts the current SDK canonical ProtoStateMachineDefinition (src/schema/fiber-app.ts:281), which uses plain-string ids; it bypasses the defineFiberApp() schema every other app uses; and it hardcodes a delegation.isAuthorized guard that exists nowhere in the SDK (delegation is in still-unmerged PRs #41/#95). The conflict is semantic, not textual, so a rebase cannot rescue it. This is a reopened #45 re-litigating a model the chain has since rewritten.
dependsOn: #41 (SDK delegation module — provides the delegation.isAuthorized authorization surface the PR's governance guards reference)
#95 (DelegationCredential proto + delegation messages — proto half of the delegation pair)
conflictsWith: ottochain asset model RFC v2 (docs/proposals/asset-model.md + modules/models/.../asset/TokenBehavior.scala) — 5-bit TSCEG lattice supersedes the PR's 4-bit TDEG model
src/schema/fiber-app.ts ProtoStateMachineDefinition — plain-string state ids vs the PR's { value: string } wrapper
docs/proposals/fiber-apps-overhaul.md — plans Treasury/Registry-asset reorg that this standalone token module ignores
alignmentGaps: Bit model mismatch: PR uses 4-bit TDEG (T=8,D=4,E=2,G=1) in src/apps/token/types.ts; chain uses 5-bit TSCEG (T=16,S=8,C=4,E=2,G=1) in ottochain/modules/models/src/main/scala/xyz/kd5ujc/schema/asset/TokenBehavior.scala. NFT=8 in PR vs 16 on chain; all 16 named archetypes and their test assertions are numerically invalid.

Representation mismatch: chain encodes behavior as a single packed Int (AssetCommit.behavior, Circe Encoder.encodeInt) and enforces structure via typed MorphismKind (Transfer/Burn/Fractionalize/Compose/Decompose/Pool/Wrap/Stake) in Scala; the PR emits a full StateMachineDefinition JSON with split/merge transitions and JSON-Logic guards.

Wire-format mismatch: src/apps/token/types.ts WireStateId { value: string } and state-machine.ts sid() contradict src/schema/fiber-app.ts:281 ProtoStateMachineDefinition where id/initialState/from/to are plain strings. No { value } StateId wrapper exists in the proto or chain.

Schema-pattern bypass: src/apps/token/state-machine.ts does not use src/schema/fiber-app.ts defineFiberApp()/toProtoDefinition() that identity/contracts/markets/governance/corporate all use; it duplicates TokenStateMachineDefinition/WireState/WireTransition types.

Dangling guard dependency: src/apps/token/state-machine.ts hardcodes GOVERNANCE_GUARD { var: 'delegation.isAuthorized' } and EXPIRY_GUARD state.expiresAtOrdinal; grep of src/ finds neither anywhere in the current SDK. Delegation lives only in unmerged #41/#95.
Missing spec: tests reference docs/design/asset-model-token-spec.md (asset-model-token-spec.md §3/§6.3) which does not exist in the repo.

Signing-canonical risk: the PR's bespoke { value: string } shape was never validated against JCS(dropNulls(payload)) per docs/signing-and-publishing.md; the chain's Int encoding is specifically chosen as 'signing-canonical-safe'.
CI regression: .github/workflows/consumer-test.yml change downgrades pnpm/action-setup v6→v4 and pins pnpm 10→9 against the current v6 config.
risks: Landing as-is would publish SDK token types whose behavior integers (NFT=8 etc.) disagree with the chain (NFT=16), so any consumer building a token would produce updates the chain rejects or mis-types.
The { value: string } StateId wire shape would diverge from the chain canonical and surface as opaque InvalidSignature/HTTP 400 if ever submitted.
Hardcoded delegation.isAuthorized guard would silently no-op (guard var unresolved) until #41/#95 land, giving a false sense of governance enforcement.
Reintroduces a duplicate state-machine type system parallel to src/schema/fiber-app.ts, increasing drift surface for future signing/canonical changes.
recommendedActions: Close PR #80 as superseded; comment linking ottochain docs/proposals/asset-model.md (RFC v2) and modules/models/.../asset/TokenBehavior.scala as the authoritative model, and reference the supersede note in that RFC §0.

If a token SDK surface is still wanted, open a fresh issue/PR to implement the 5-bit TSCEG model + MorphismKind verbs as a thin typed mirror of the chain: a packed-Int behavior (encode to Int, not a StateMachineDefinition), built on src/schema/fiber-app.ts defineFiberApp()/toProtoDefinition(), aligned with the Treasury/Registry plan in docs/proposals/fiber-apps-overhaul.md.
Sequence any new token work AFTER the delegation pair (#41 module + #95 proto) lands so governance guards reference a real delegation.isAuthorized surface instead of a hardcoded var.
Do not cherry-pick the .github/workflows/consumer-test.yml hunk from this PR — it would regress pnpm/action-setup v6→v4 and pnpm 10→9.

Salvage value: the 16-test-per-archetype structure and event-builder ergonomics (createTransferEvent/validateTokenEvent) are reusable patterns; carry the testing approach forward, discard the TDEG numerics and { value } wire types.

alignment.summary: The SDK's core signing mechanism — dropNulls + RFC8785/JCS — is correctly aligned with metakit's current JsonBinaryCodec. src/ottochain/drop-nulls.ts byte-matches JsonBinaryCodec.dropNulls (recursively drop null OBJECT fields, preserve array nulls), and signing.ts/verify.ts apply it internally and unconditionally in dataUpdate mode, which is exactly what metakit's content-hash.md (post the 2026-06-10 e2e incident) requires; the content-hash doc even names the SDK's dropNulls as a cross-language conformance target. No divergence in dropNulls ordering or array-null handling. The new sigma (Σ-protocol) opcodes do NOT affect the signing surface: they are JLVM evaluation opcodes used inside guards/effects (prove_dlog_verify, prove_dhtuple_verify, sigma_verify), and no proof-carrying fields were added to any DataUpdate schema on the ottochain side — confirmed by grep across modules/models. The real, high-severity divergences are NOT in the crypto/canonical layer but in the registry SIGNED-MESSAGE SCHEMA, which the SDK has not tracked: (1) the chain split the single PublishVersion into PublishMachineVersion + PublishScriptVersion with restructured shape fields (machineShape/scriptShape + scriptProgram) and replaced SchemaShape with the MachineShape/ScriptShape/RegistryShape ADT, while the SDK still ships one PublishVersion{schemaShape, definition}; and (2) the chain made strict / FieldShape.repeated / FieldShape.optional non-defaulted required Boolean fields, while the SDK types them optional+omittable — a direct violation of the chain's signing-canonical invariant #1 and the SDK's own docs/signing-and-publishing.md rule 2. A secondary soft gap: metakit enforces a JSON depth limit (DefaultMaxDepth=64) that the SDK does not mirror.

findings.topic: JSON nesting depth limit not mirrored in SDK

alignment.summary: The OttoChain metagraph is entirely app-agnostic: on-chain it only knows `StateMachineDefinition { states: Map[StateId,State], initialState, transitions: List[Transition], metadata }` (modules/models/.../schema/fiber/StateMachineDefinition.scala), `State { id, isFinal, metadata }`, and `Transition { from, to, eventName, guard, effect, dependencies: Set[UUID] }`. It has NO concept of identity/governance/markets/treasury/registry apps, no `createSchema`/`stateSchema`/`eventSchemas`/`definitions`, no `emits` on transitions, and no `$timestamp` context key. The SDK `FiberAppDefinition` (src/schema/fiber-app.ts) plus the app definitions (src/apps/*) layer a much richer schema on top. The bridging path `toProtoDefinition()` is meant to strip down to the chain shape but is opt-in and itself buggy, and several app definitions use constructs (`emits`, object-form `dependencies`, `$timestamp`) that the chain ignores, rejects, or resolves to null. The unimplemented overhaul (treasury/registry apps, generated types, proto-enum-validation CI) has zero on-chain counterpart and never needs one because the chain is app-agnostic; the SDK-side Phase-1 refactor (oracles->identity, corporate consolidation, universal+specialized) is partly done but the generation/validation tooling from fiber-app-schema.md is absent, so nothing guards these divergences. The chain validators (FiberRules/FiberValidator) and the authoritative SdkCompatibilitySuite + JsonEncodedStateMachineSuite fixtures define the real wire contract and were used to verify each finding.

findings.topic: Transition.dependencies: object DependencySpec vs chain Set[UUID]

Corporate machines (corp-entity.ts L476-480, L646-655; also corp-board/corp-securities/corp-shareholders) actually emit object-form dependencies. toProtoDefinition() spreads them through unchanged (fiber-app.ts L322).
findings.chainState: modules/models/.../fiber/Transition.scala: `dependencies: Set[UUID]`. The chain decoder (Circe customizableDecoder) decodes each element as a UUID. Chain's own fixtures (JsonEncodedStateMachineSuite L417/444 etc., SdkCompatibilitySuite L71) ALWAYS send dependencies as arrays of UUID strings, never objects. The runtime ContextProvider.buildMachinesContext consumes `Set[UUID]` to inject `machines`/`scripts` context.

Any CreateStateMachine carrying such a definition is rejected at the chain decoder (or fails verification), and `requiredState`/`instanceRef` semantics simply do not exist on-chain — there is no declarative cross-machine state precondition; dependencies only seed read-only context. The corporate app definitions are categorically un-submittable as written.

Either remove DependencySpec from the wire-bound Transition type or have toProtoDefinition reject/transform non-string dependencies. Add a unit test asserting every app definition's toProtoDefinition output has dependencies as string[] only.

findings.topic: Transition.emits declared statically in SDK; chain has no emits field
findings.sdkState: fiber-app.ts Transition.emits: `readonly (string | EmitSpec)[]`. 8 corporate/governance machines declare `emits: ["CORPORATION_FORMED"]` etc. (corp-entity.ts L467/512/599/...). toProtoDefinition() does NOT strip emits, so it would ride the signed definition.
findings.chainState: Transition.scala has NO emits field. Event emission is a RUNTIME effect convention: the effect result writes the reserved `_emit` key (ReservedKeys.EMIT) parsed by parseEmittedEvent (NAME/DATA/DESTINATION). The chain decoder drops the unknown `emits` field on decode (useDefaults config ignores unknown keys).
findings.gap: Two problems: (1) the static `emits` declaration is purely informational and is never honored by the chain — emission only happens if the effect body produces `_emit`, which none of these SDK definitions do, so the declared events never fire; (2) if a caller signs the full definition (with emits present) the chain re-encodes WITHOUT emits, breaking the signing canonical (InvalidSignature) — see finding on canonical mismatch.
findings.recommendation: Either (a) drop `emits` from the wire Transition and keep it as documentation-only metadata stripped by toProtoDefinition, or (b) generate the corresponding `_emit` effect output from the `emits` declaration so the runtime actually emits. Add tests confirming toProtoDefinition output contains no `emits` key, and that declared emits correspond to a real `_emit` in the effect.

findings.sdkState: FiberAppDefinition includes createSchema, stateSchema, eventSchemas, definitions, plus per-transition emits and per-state metadata convention. createStateMachinePayload (src/ottochain/transaction.ts L57-66) accepts an opaque `definition: Record<string,unknown>` and signs whatever it's given. toProtoDefinition() exists to extract the {states,initialState,transitions,metadata} subset but is OPT-IN; nothing forces callers to use it.
findings.chainState: StateMachineDefinition has only {states, initialState, transitions, metadata}. CodecConfiguration uses `Configuration.default.withDefaults`, so the decoder silently IGNORES unknown keys (createSchema/eventSchemas/etc.). On verify, the chain re-encodes the decoded StateMachineDefinition WITHOUT those fields. Signing must reproduce JCS(dropNulls(payload)) exactly (docs/signing) or it is rejected InvalidSignature.
findings.gap: If any caller passes a raw FiberAppDefinition (or anything beyond the 4 chain fields) to createStateMachinePayload, the signed canonical includes extra keys that the chain's re-encoded canonical lacks -> InvalidSignature (opaque HTTP 400). The SDK ships rich definitions and an opt-in stripper but no guardrail tying the two together.
findings.recommendation: Have createStateMachinePayload run definitions through toProtoDefinition() (or a strict allowlist of {states,initialState,transitions,metadata}) before signing, OR type its `definition` param as ProtoStateMachineDefinition instead of Record<string,unknown>. Add a signing parity test that round-trips a real app definition through toProtoDefinition and asserts byte-for-byte JCS(dropNulls()) equality against the Scala StateMachineDefinition canonical (mirror SdkCompatibilitySuite).

findings.topic: toProtoDefinition passes FiberAppMetadata as StateMachineDefinition.metadata
findings.sdkState: fiber-app.ts toProtoDefinition L335-337: `if (def.metadata) protoDef.metadata = def.metadata`. But FiberAppDefinition.metadata is FiberAppMetadata {name, app, type, version, description, category, crossReferences} — app-routing info, not state-machine metadata. There is no top-level state-machine metadata field on FiberAppDefinition.
findings.chainState: StateMachineDefinition.metadata: Option[JsonLogicValue] = None — a free-form on-chain metadata blob, expected to be either absent (null, dropped) or a plain JSON object. Chain stores it but does not interpret app/type/version.
findings.gap: toProtoDefinition injects SDK app-routing metadata (name/app/type/version) into the on-chain state-machine metadata slot. This is semantically wrong (app routing leaks into chain metadata) and, more importantly, it makes the on-chain canonical depend on SDK packaging fields — changing description/category/crossReferences would change the signed digest and the registry logicHash even though the executable machine is identical.
findings.recommendation: Decide explicitly what belongs in StateMachineDefinition.metadata. Either omit it entirely from toProtoDefinition (recommended — keep app metadata off-chain), or project only a stable, intentional subset. Do not pass the full FiberAppMetadata object. Add a test pinning the exact metadata shape that reaches the wire.

findings.topic: $timestamp context variable used pervasively but absent on-chain
findings.sdkState: 20 of the SDK state machines (~150+ occurrences) use `{var: "$timestamp"}` in effects to stamp fields like activatedAt/suspendedAt/createdAt (e.g. identity-agent.ts L206, contract-agreement, dao-*, market-*).
findings.chainState: ContextProvider.buildContextData (ContextProvider.scala L160-178) injects ONLY: state, event, eventName, machineId, currentStateId, sequenceNumber, $ordinal, $lastSnapshotHash, $epochProgress, proofs, machines, parent, children, scripts, heldAssets. ReservedKeys defines ORDINAL/EPOCH_PROGRESS/LAST_SNAPSHOT_HASH but NO $timestamp. JsonLogic `var` on a missing key resolves to null.
findings.gap: Every effect field set from `$timestamp` will be written as null on-chain (no error, silent). Computed timestamp fields the SDK schema marks `computed: true` (activatedAt, suspendedAt, probationStartedAt, etc.) will always be null in actual fiber state, diverging from SDK/explorer expectations and breaking any guard/ordering logic that compares against a timestamp.
findings.recommendation: Replace `$timestamp` with the chain-provided deterministic ordering key `$ordinal` (or $epochProgress) throughout the app effects, and update the stateSchema field types/descriptions accordingly (ordinal is an integer, not an ISO timestamp). If wall-clock time is truly needed, raise it with the chain team to add a deterministic time key to ContextProvider — but until then, the SDK must stop emitting $timestamp. Add a lint/test that fails if any app effect references a var not in the chain's reserved-context allowlist.

findings.topic: Redundant `status` field in effects vs chain-tracked currentState
findings.sdkState: Effects write a `status` field into stateData mirroring the target state (identity-agent.ts: `{status:"ACTIVE",...}`), and stateSchema.status is an enum of the state ids marked computed.
findings.chainState: FiberEvaluator sets `newStateId = Some(transition.to)` (FiberEvaluator.scala L268); the canonical current state is the fiber record's currentState, independent of any stateData `status` field. The chain never reads a `status` key to determine state.
findings.gap: Two sources of truth for lifecycle state: chain `currentState` (authoritative) and an SDK-authored `status` field inside stateData. They can silently diverge if an effect forgets to set status, or if a transition's `to` differs from the status it writes. Not a hard break, but a correctness/consistency footgun and extra signed bytes.
findings.recommendation: Drop the redundant `status` writes from effects and have consumers read the chain's currentState (exposed via the fiber record) as the single source of truth, or add a test asserting every transition's effect status equals transition.to. At minimum document that `status` is advisory and currentState wins.

findings.topic: dependencies omitted-when-empty vs chain requiredness (toProtoDefinition)
findings.sdkState: toProtoDefinition L322 omits `dependencies` when empty, with a comment claiming 'dependencies has default Set.empty in Scala'.
findings.chainState: Transition.scala `dependencies: Set[UUID]` has NO Scala default. With `useDefaults` the decoder can fall back ONLY where a default exists; for dependencies there is none, so an absent key relies on Circe/magnolia treating a missing Set as empty. The chain's own fixtures (SdkCompatibilitySuite L71, JsonEncodedStateMachineSuite) ALWAYS send `dependencies: []` explicitly.
findings.gap: The SDK comment is inaccurate (no Scala default), and omitting the key diverges from every chain reference fixture which sends `[]`. Whether omission decodes cleanly depends on magnolia's empty-collection handling; the canonical the chain re-encodes will contain `dependencies: []`, so if the SDK signed a payload that OMITTED it, the canonical would mismatch unless dropNulls/empty-handling happens to align.
findings.recommendation: Always emit `dependencies: []` (matching the chain fixtures and the re-encoded canonical) rather than omitting it, and fix the misleading comment. Verify with a signing-parity test that the SDK transition canonical (empty deps) equals the Scala Transition canonical.

findings.topic: No client-side guard against reserved-operator field names
findings.sdkState: SDK has no validation preventing a definition from using a JSON Logic operator name (merge, map, count, min, max, in, get, has, keys, values, length, cat, default, find, etc.) as a DATA key inside guard/effect map literals. Authoring is freehand JSON-Logic in the .ts files.
findings.chainState: FiberRules.L1.noReservedOperatorFieldNames REJECTS (ReservedOperatorAsFieldName) any definition whose guard/effect MapExpression keys collide with JsonLogicOp.knownOperatorTags. Current SDK apps happen to use operator names only in operator position (legal), so they pass today — verified across contracts/markets/governance.
findings.gap: The chain enforces a rule the SDK does not mirror. A future app field named e.g. `count`, `min`, or `merge` as a data key would be silently authored, pass SDK type-checking, then be rejected on-chain. No tooling catches this pre-submit.
findings.recommendation: Port the reserved-operator-key check into defineFiberApp() (or a build-time validator / the proposed generate-app-types.mjs) using the same JsonLogicOp tag list from metakit, so collisions fail fast at SDK build time instead of at chain ingestion.

findings.topic: Overhaul + schema-generation proposals: SDK partially done, zero on-chain counterpart
findings.sdkState: Phase-1 of fiber-apps-overhaul.md is partially reflected in the SDK: oracles/ is a deprecated shim absorbed into identity (identity-oracle), corporate is consolidated, markets/governance follow universal+specialized. But Phase-3 apps (treasury, registry) are ABSENT from src/apps, and fiber-app-schema.md's tooling (generate-app-types.mjs, types.generated.ts, transitions.generated.ts, dist/schemas/*.json, validate-proto-enums.mjs CI) is NOT implemented — schemas are handwritten in fiber-app.ts/apps/*.
findings.chainState: The chain is fully app-agnostic: grep of modules/models for treasury/registry-as-app/identity/governance/createSchema/eventSchemas finds nothing (only registry as the version/package system, unrelated to the SDK 'registry app' proposal). The chain only ever sees StateMachineDefinition. There is no proto enum per app on-chain to validate against.
findings.gap: The overhaul and schema-generation proposals are SDK/tooling concerns with no on-chain analogue — the chain neither needs nor reflects them, so there is no 'chain side' to align for new apps. The risk is purely SDK-internal: without the proposed generation/validation (proto-enum-vs-states CI, reserved-key lint, signing-parity tests), the divergences in the other findings have no automated guardrail. The proto-enum-validation premise in fiber-app-schema.md is partly moot since the chain stores states as free-form StateId strings, not proto enums.
findings.recommendation: Close the proposals' status: mark the overhaul Phase-1 'done (no on-chain work required, chain is app-agnostic)', defer/abandon treasury+registry until needed, and re-scope fiber-app-schema.md around what actually protects the chain contract — (1) a toProtoDefinition signing-parity test against the Scala canonical, (2) a reserved-context-var allowlist lint ($timestamp etc.), (3) a reserved-operator-key lint, (4) a dependencies-shape check. Drop the proto-enum-validation idea or redirect it to validate states against the registry MachineShape projection instead.

protocols.protocol: Midnight (IOG / Midnight Foundation) implementing the Kachina model (Kerber, Kiayias, Kohlweiss; IACR ePrint 2020/543). Kachina is the formal "private smart contract = public on-chain state + private off-chain state + transition function proven by NIZK" framework, proven secure in the UC model. Midnight is its production instantiation: Compact (DSL) -> ZK circuits + Impact VM (on-chain stack VM that replays the public transcript), with Zswap (ePrint 2022/1002) as the shielded-asset layer. NIGHT token launched on Cardano Dec 8 2025 (Hilo); privacy dApp mainnet (Kukolu) staged for Q1 2026. Compact was contributed to Linux Foundation Decentralized Trust as the "Minokawa" project.
protocols.proofSystem: Kachina the PAPER is proof-system-agnostic: it requires only a general-purpose NIZK/zk-SNARK with simulation-extractability for an arbitrary relation R linking (public-state delta, public transcript) to a witness (private state, private inputs); it does NOT specify a scheme and imposes no setup at the abstraction level. Midnight the IMPLEMENTATION uses `midnight-proofs`, a fork of PSE's Halo2 (lineage Zcash Sapling -> PSE Halo2 v0.3.0): PLONKish arithmetization with KZG polynomial commitments (Pluto-Eris / formerly BLS12-381, Poseidon + in-circuit SHA256, 128-bit truncated Fiat-Shamir for recursion). Zswap uses Zcash-friendly simulation-extractable zk-SNARKs. CRITICAL for OttoChain: this is GENERAL-PURPOSE circuit-satisfiability SNARK machinery, NOT a Schnorr/Sigma system. OttoChain has ONLY Sigma-protocols (ProveDlog / ProveDHTuple / AND-OR proof trees, Fiat-Shamir) which prove fixed algebraic statements (knowledge of discrete logs, DH-tuples, monotone access structures) and CANNOT prove arbitrary JLVM circuit execution. So Kachina's core proving engine cannot be reproduced with Sigma alone. Note on setup: Kachina abstractly needs none (any NIZK, incl. transparent); Midnight's KZG path requires a universal/updatable powers-of-tau SRS.
protocols.stateModel: Two-part state per contract. (1) PUBLIC state on-chain in the shared ledger; in Compact this is the `ledger` declaration (typed ADT fields -- counters, Merkle trees, sets, maps -- manipulated by the Impact VM, a stack-based VM that replays the public transcript). (2) PRIVATE state held OFF-CHAIN, locally per user, never published. In Kachina the private state is accessed only INDIRECTLY through a contract-defined "state oracle"; a contract is formally a transition function plus a leakage function. In Compact private data enters via `witness` functions (return a value AND an updated private state via WitnessContext{ledger, privateState, address}); everything derived from a witness is "private by default" and must be explicitly disclosed to cross into public state. The chain stores NO private state and NO global private-state tree -- privacy state is sharded per user; only commitments the contract chooses to bind (e.g. a Merkle-root/commitment ledger field) appear on-chain.
protocols.offchainOnchainSplit: Off-chain: the user runs the transition locally against their private state, producing (i) a PUBLIC TRANSCRIPT = ordered operations/queries against the public-state oracle (what the chain replays), (ii) a PRIVATE TRANSCRIPT = witness outputs consumed only by the prover, (iii) a public-state delta. A proof server then generates a NIZK that there EXISTS a private state + private inputs making the public transcript a valid execution of the contract transition. On-chain settlement: tx carries {public transcript, public-state delta, proof}; validators verify the proof and the Impact VM re-executes the public transcript against current on-chain state -- commits iff the transcript read-set still matches, else reject/rebase. This transcript-replay IS Kachina's concurrency mechanism: the state-oracle transcript records dependencies so non-conflicting txs commute and reorder, and the contract author controls (via the oracle) what must be proven and what counts as a conflict, minimizing proof size and leakage. The Impact transcript is conceptually the same artifact as a deterministic JLVM state-machine transition log.
protocols.trustSetup: Universal/updatable trusted setup required in the Midnight instantiation (KZG SRS via powers-of-tau). The Kachina abstraction itself imposes no setup -- any NIZK works, including transparent ones. Halo2's IPA variant is transparent, but midnight-proofs deliberately chose the KZG path for succinct/constant-size proofs and recursion, accepting the ceremony. Schnorr/Sigma-protocols (OttoChain) are transparent / setup-free -- strictly better on this axis, but only for the narrow class of statements Sigma can express.
protocols.assetPrivacy: Zswap (ePrint 2022/1002): a Zerocash-style shielded UTXO/note model. Each coin is a NOTE committed on-chain via a COMMITMENT in a Merkle tree; spending reveals a deterministic NULLIFIER (from note + secret) to block double-spends, with a zk-SNARK proving the spent note is in the commitment tree and the nullifier is well-formed without revealing which note. Multi-asset + atomic swaps: SPARSE HOMOMORPHIC (multi-value Pedersen) COMMITMENTS to (value,type) pairs that SUM across a tx so balance is checked homomorphically; relaxed/aggregated signatures let independent shielded txs be MERGED into one atomic balanced multi-asset swap non-interactively. This asset-privacy primitive is distinct from the general Kachina contract layer and itself depends on a general SNARK for the spend circuit.
protocols.programmability: Fully general. Kachina's transition function is arbitrary computation over public+private state; Compact is a statically-typed TypeScript-flavored DSL compiling to ZK circuits, with the compiler auto-splitting code into on-chain (Impact VM ops on the ledger ADT), off-chain (witness/private-state) and in-circuit (proof) parts. It can express arbitrary state machines, access control, private voting, identity/credentials, DEX logic. The ONLY hard limit is circuit encodability (bounded loops, fixed circuit per exported entry point). This generality of HIDDEN logic is a property of the general SNARK, NOT of the Kachina architecture per se -- precisely what a Sigma-only system lacks.
protocols.maturity: Production-staging as of mid-2026. NIGHT token live on Cardano mainnet since Dec 8 2025 (Hilo phase); federated privacy-dApp mainnet (Kukolu) targeted Q1 2026 for the first wave of production apps. Compact + Impact VM + Zswap are implemented and documented; midnight-proofs is a published Rust crate (v0.7.0). Compact donated to Linux Foundation Decentralized Trust as "Minokawa". Underlying theory (Kachina UC-proven; Zswap PETS 2022) is peer-reviewed. Net: research-mature and engineering-mature, just entering production traffic -- more mature than most ZK-contract competitors.
protocols.relevance: VERY HIGH as a reference architecture, MODERATE as a directly-copyable blueprint, because OttoChain lacks the general SNARK that Kachina/Midnight depend on. Kachina is the canonical formalization of exactly what "privately managed off-chain fibers" want to be: a private off-chain state machine whose public effects settle on-chain via a verifiable transcript. Its decomposition (public ledger state + per-user private state + transition function + public-transcript replay for concurrency + explicit leakage function as the privacy budget) is the right mental model and maps cleanly onto OttoChain primitives: JLVM state machines ARE transition functions; the deterministic JCS(dropNulls) canonicalization IS the transcript-equality/replay-determinism guarantee Kachina needs; the Rust/TS/Scala byte-for-byte parity IS the multi-party re-execution Kachina assumes. The GAP is purely the proof: Kachina/Midnight prove an ARBITRARY private transition with a general circuit SNARK; OttoChain has only Sigma-protocols proving fixed algebraic relations. So OttoChain can borrow the ARCHITECTURE and the CONCURRENCY/TRANSCRIPT model directly, and can build a meaningful subset of private fibers whose hidden predicate reduces to Sigma-expressible statements, but CANNOT (without adding a general SNARK) hide arbitrary JLVM transition logic the way Compact does.
protocols.family: ZK private-smart-contract family -- Kachina lineage (public+private state, NIZK-proven off-chain transition, transcript settlement). Siblings/contrasts: Zexe/VeriZexe, Aleo/snarkVM, Aztec/Noir, Zcash/Zerocash (asset-only). Distinct from FHE-based privacy (smartFHE) and from MPC. OttoChain's Sigma-only stack is closest in spirit to Zerocash-era / Ergo Sigma-protocol systems -- a strict expressiveness subset of the Kachina family.
patternsToBorrow: Public/private state split with per-user OFF-CHAIN private state and NO global private-state tree on chain -- directly applicable to off-chain fibers: the metagraph stores only public fiber state + commitments.

Transcript-replay settlement = Kachina state-oracle transcript: have an off-chain fiber emit a deterministic PUBLIC transcript of its reads/writes against public state; the metagraph re-executes via JLVM and commits iff the read-set still matches. OttoChain already has the deterministic JLVM + JCS(dropNulls) canonical replay needed to make this byte-for-byte sound -- highest-value borrowable pattern, needs NO SNARK.
Optimistic concurrency via explicit read/write dependency sets in the transcript, so non-conflicting fiber transitions commute and can be reordered/rebased instead of serialized.

Explicit LEAKAGE FUNCTION as a first-class privacy budget: force each fiber transition to declare exactly what public info it discloses (Compact 'private by default + explicit disclosure'). A design discipline borrowable regardless of proof system.

Commit-and-settle with commitments + nullifiers for the cases Sigma CAN handle: a Pedersen/EC commitment to private state, opened/transitioned with a Schnorr/ProveDlog proof; single-use/double-spend enforcement via a deterministic nullifier whose well-formedness is a ProveDHTuple statement. Gives Zswap-style note spending and private membership WITHOUT a general SNARK (anonymity set limited by one-out-of-many/ring scaling).

Verification-key-as-contract-identity (Midnight): bind a fiber's on-chain identity to a hash of its JLVM program / its Sigma verification parameters, so invoking the fiber means submitting a proof against its fixed statement.

AND-OR Sigma proof trees for private access control / threshold authorization inside a fiber (private voting thresholds, m-of-n approval, disjunctive credential proofs) -- the native sweet spot of OttoChain's sigma opcodes, mapping onto governance/corporate/identity apps.
Off-chain proof-server / local-prover architecture: keep witness (secret-key) material on the user's machine; the chain only ever sees public transcript + proof.
pitfalls: DO NOT assume Sigma-protocols can replace the Kachina/Midnight SNARK. Sigma proves fixed algebraic statements (discrete logs, DH-tuples, monotone AND/OR); it CANNOT prove 'this arbitrary JLVM/JSON-Logic transition executed correctly on hidden inputs.' Hiding arbitrary fiber logic requires general circuit satisfiability you don't have.

Trusted-setup mismatch: Midnight's KZG path needs a powers-of-tau ceremony. If OttoChain ever adds SNARKs to close the gap, prefer transparent systems (Bulletproofs/STARKs/IPA-Halo2) to preserve the setup-free property Sigma gives today; don't silently inherit a ceremony.

Transcript determinism is load-bearing: Kachina concurrency/soundness assume the public transcript replays IDENTICALLY across validators. Any nondeterminism in JLVM evaluation or canonicalization across Rust/TS/Scala (exactly what JCS(dropNulls) guards) breaks settlement with opaque failures -- same class as the InvalidSignature/HTTP-400 canonical-mismatch already known in the SDK.

Leakage is subtle: even with proofs, the public transcript + which oracle entries are touched + tx timing/size leak. Sigma proofs are larger/non-succinct vs SNARKs and can leak statement structure; designing each fiber's leakage function to actually minimize this is hard and must be explicit.

Asset privacy (Zswap) relies on a SNARK proving Merkle membership of the spent note. A pure-Sigma version only works if membership is a Sigma-friendly statement (one-out-of-many / ring proofs), which scales worse -- anonymity-set size is a real constraint.

Don't conflate Kachina (general contract layer) with Zswap (asset layer); they are separate constructions, and 'private payments' means importing Zswap's note model, which again leans on a general SNARK for the spend circuit.

Compact/Halo2 give bounded-loop, fixed-circuit-per-entrypoint semantics; a JSON-Logic state machine is more dynamic. Mapping dynamic JLVM control flow into any fixed proving statement (SNARK or Sigma) forces bounding/unrolling decisions.

protocols.protocol: Aztec Network (Noir / Aztec.nr) — privacy-first zkRollup L2 on Ethereum. Hybrid private/public smart contracts; dev surface is aztec.js + PXE, contracts written in Noir via the Aztec.nr framework.
protocols.proofSystem: Recursive SNARK stack, NOT a Σ-protocol. Client side: each private function call is one step of a ClientIVC (Incrementally Verifiable Computation) chain folded with Protogalaxy; proven with the Honk family (UltraHonk = PLONK-arithmetised circuits proved via Sumcheck over multilinear polynomials + Shplemini/Gemini+Shplonk PCS opening). Goblin Plonk / ECCVM (over Grumpkin) + Translator (over BN254) defer non-native EC ops across recursion (BN254/Grumpkin curve cycle). Rollup side recursively verifies Honk proofs; one compression layer wraps the final proof in an UltraPlonk circuit for cheap on-chain (Ethereum L1) verification via a KZG/pairing verifier. Hashing is Poseidon2, enshrined protocol-wide. This is a general-purpose SNARK toolchain (arbitrary PLONKish circuits), categorically more powerful — and far heavier — than Schnorr/Σ-protocol opcodes.
protocols.trustSetup: YES — required. KZG polynomial commitments need a universal (updatable) SRS over the pairing-friendly BN254 curve; the final UltraPlonk wrapper is a zkSNARK with a universal trusted setup. Aztec reuses an existing universal Powers-of-Tau-style ceremony (one-time, updatable, 1-of-n honest assumption). The inner Honk/IPA path over Grumpkin (ECCVM) is transparent (Inner Product Argument, no setup), but the on-chain settlement path still bottoms out in KZG with a trusted SRS. Contrast: OttoChain's Σ-protocol opcodes (ProveDlog/ProveDHTuple + Fiat-Shamir) need NO trusted setup at all — keep that as an advantage, not a gap.
protocols.stateModel: Dual state. PRIVATE state = UTXO-style "notes": encrypted data packets owned by an address. Only the note COMMITMENT (a Poseidon2 hash of the note preimage, siloed by contract address and a per-tx nonce so every leaf is unique) is inserted into an append-only "note hash tree" (Merkle). Notes are never deleted. To consume/spend a note you emit a NULLIFIER — a deterministic value derived from (note data, owner nullifier-secret, storage slot) via poseidon2_hash_with_separator — inserted into a separate "nullifier tree." Double-spend prevention = uniqueness check in the nullifier tree; because the nullifier requires the owner's secret key, observers cannot link a note to its nullifier (unlinkability). Updating private state = nullify old note(s) + create new note(s) (cash/change analogy). PUBLIC state = transparent account/slot key-value in a "public data tree," exactly like Ethereum, mutated by the Aztec VM (AVM). The note+nullifier+commitment-tree topology is OttoChain's closest analog target, but here every commitment/nullifier validity is enforced INSIDE a SNARK circuit, not by a chain-side JLVM guard.
protocols.offchainOnchainSplit: Private execution runs entirely client-side in the PXE ("Private eXecution Environment," a local wallet service); raw private data never leaves the device. PXE simulates each private function (ACIR simulator) producing PrivateCircuitPublicInputs, then the recursive private KERNEL circuit folds/verifies each function call's proof into one transaction proof. Published to the sequencer = the tx proof + public inputs: new note hashes (commitments), new nullifiers, encrypted note/event LOGS (ciphertext only), enqueued public-function calls, and fee info — all opaque ("public but encrypted; tells you nothing about what happened"). Ordering rule: private execution ALWAYS precedes public; private fns can enqueue public calls, not vice-versa. The sequencer runs enqueued PUBLIC functions in the AVM (public, deterministic, sequencer-executed), inserts the commitments/nullifiers into the trees, and ROLLUP circuits recursively verify all kernel proofs + advance tree snapshots; the compressed proof settles on Ethereum L1. So: off-chain = produce state transition + correctness proof; on-chain = verify proof, append commitments, insert nullifiers, advance roots. The settlement transcript is commitments + nullifiers + ciphertext logs + a succinct validity proof — which maps directly onto an OttoChain off-chain fiber emitting (new state commitment, nullifier, Σ-proof bundle) for the JLVM guard to re-verify.
protocols.assetPrivacy: Tokens are notes (encrypted UTXOs) holding (amount, owner). Transfers nullify the sender's input notes and create new value+change notes encrypted to recipient/sender; amounts and the sender↔recipient link stay hidden because notes are ciphertext and nullifiers are unlinkable without the owner's nullifier key. Recipients find incoming notes by trial-decrypting the published encrypted logs with their viewing keys. Key hierarchy separates nullifier, incoming-viewing, and outgoing-viewing keys. A token can also expose a PUBLIC balance (public-data-tree slot); private↔public conversion is explicit (shield/unshield). Anonymity set = the whole note hash tree. Critically, balance conservation (inputs == outputs, amounts non-negative) is enforced by in-circuit RANGE/arithmetic constraints, NOT by a transparent guard — this is the part Σ-protocols alone cannot reproduce.
protocols.programmability: High / Turing-expressive within circuit limits. Contracts are written in Noir (a Rust-like zk DSL) via Aztec.nr: arbitrary private functions (compiled to ACIR constraint systems), public functions (AVM bytecode), cross-function/cross-contract composability, and explicit private↔public messaging. Arbitrary app logic and state machines ARE expressible — but private logic must be fixed-shape circuits: no unbounded loops, constrained data-dependent control flow, and everything a private fn reads must be provable client-side (it can read historical/immutable state, not live mutable public state at private-proving time). For OttoChain: state machines are expressible here, but private branches are compiled circuits, whereas OttoChain's are interpreted-at-runtime JSON-Logic — so the "prove arbitrary private execution" capability does not carry over with Σ-protocols only.
protocols.maturity: Alpha / experimental, decentralizing. Public testnet through 2024–2025; the community-operated "Ignition" L2 chain went live Nov 2025 (Aztec 2.0 line) with permissionless sequencers/provers (3,500+ sequencers cited) settling to Ethereum L1. Explicitly labeled early/experimental software with "known vulnerabilities," launched without full external audit (audits planned alongside the move to UltraPlonk; bug bounty active). Proof stack mid-migration (TurboPlonk → UltraPlonk/UltraHonk). Not yet a hardened, finalized mainnet as of mid-2026; production-grade guarantees still maturing.
patternsToBorrow: Commitment + nullifier set as THE privacy primitive: store only a Poseidon-style hash commitment of off-chain fiber state in an append-only tree, plus a separate nullifier set to retire/transition it. Implementable with Σ-protocols ONLY — the nullifier can be a key-bound value where the owner proves in ZK (ProveDlog, Fiat-Shamir) knowledge of secret x with pubkey g^x and correct nullifier derivation. Highest-value borrowable pattern for OttoChain's private off-chain fibers; no trusted setup needed.

Unlinkability via key-derived nullifiers: derive the spend/transition tag from the owner's secret key so observers can't link state record -> nullifier. ProveDHTuple expresses a verifiable PRF-style binding of the nullifier to the secret key (equality-of-discrete-logs), a known Σ-friendly construction.

Off-chain-compute / on-chain-verify settlement shape: client produces new state + short transcript; chain only verifies and appends commitments + nullifiers and advances a root. OttoChain mirror: a private off-chain JLVM fiber evaluates the state machine locally, emits (new state commitment, nullifier, non-interactive Σ-proof bundle) that a public JLVM guard re-verifies via the new sigma opcodes on settlement.
Separation of viewing / spending / nullifier keys so disclosure (auditability) and spend authority are independent — fully realizable with plain EC keypairs + Σ-protocols.

Private state as UTXO notes with an explicit shield/unshield boundary to public state — maps onto OttoChain's split of script fibers (callable; can hold the private note path) vs state-machine fibers (public settlement), with conversion as an explicit transition.

Append-only commitment tree + Merkle membership for 'this note existed': membership proven against a published root. The Merkle authentication can be checked directly by the JLVM (no SNARK for the tree itself); only hiding the committed preimage needs a Σ-proof of knowledge of preimage.
pitfalls: Aztec's CORRECTNESS (no value creation, guard satisfaction, correct state transition) is enforced inside a GENERAL SNARK circuit. Σ-protocols only prove algebraic statements about discrete logs / DH tuples (knowledge of secret, equality of DLs, AND/OR trees). They cannot, alone, prove 'I ran this arbitrary JSON-Logic state machine and got this output.' The 'prove arbitrary private app logic off-chain' capability is NOT borrowable without a general SNARK OttoChain deliberately lacks.

Hidden-amount validity (private balance conservation: inputs == outputs, amount >= 0) needs RANGE PROOFS + homomorphic/Pedersen commitments. Plain Schnorr/ProveDlog gives no range proofs; you'd need Bulletproofs-style machinery. Σ-opcodes alone do NOT deliver Aztec-style confidential amounts.

Fully private CONTROL FLOW (data-dependent branches whose very existence is hidden) requires circuit-level execution. With Σ-protocols you can hide WHICH branch of an AND/OR proof tree was satisfied, but not an arbitrary computation trace — the public JLVM guard still sees the statement shape. Expect a weaker privacy model: hide secrets/keys/witnesses/owners, not the program structure.

Recursive proof aggregation / IVC (folding many calls into one succinct tx proof) is SNARK-only. Σ-proofs compose via AND/OR trees but do not compress — N statements ~ O(N) proof size. Multi-step off-chain fibers won't get Aztec's succinct single-proof settlement.
Trusted-setup envy: Aztec needs a universal SRS; the Σ-stack needs none. Do NOT copy KZG/SRS assumptions — preserve the transparent Σ advantage.

Nullifier privacy depends on a collision-resistant, key-binding hash AND byte-exact canonicalization. OttoChain must derive nullifiers via the SAME canonical path (JCS(dropNulls) + a fixed hash) byte-for-byte across Rust/TS/Scala, or a client-computed nullifier won't match the chain's recomputation — same failure class as the InvalidSignature canonical-mismatch problem.

Encrypted-log discovery (recipients scanning to find their notes) needs an encryption + note-tagging scheme + client scanning infra; orthogonal to Σ-protocols and real engineering surface (key management, tagging) that must be built regardless.
protocols.relevance: HIGH as a design template, MEDIUM as a directly-copyable mechanism. Aztec answers exactly the question OttoChain is asking — private off-chain state machines settling on-chain — and its commitment+nullifier+settlement-root architecture is the canonical reference. BORROWABLE with Σ-protocols ONLY: (1) store an off-chain fiber's private state as a hash COMMITMENT in an append-only tree; (2) retire/transition it via a key-derived NULLIFIER set for unlinkable replay/double-spend protection, authorizing with ProveDlog/ProveDHTuple + Fiat-Shamir; (3) settle off-chain compute by having the public JLVM guard re-verify a non-interactive Σ-proof bundle via the new sigma opcodes — no trusted setup, fitting OttoChain's transparent model. Clean, novel sweet spot. NOT borrowable (needs a general SNARK OttoChain lacks): proving arbitrary private JLVM execution traces, confidential AMOUNTS with range proofs, fully hidden control flow, and succinct recursive aggregation. Guidance: adopt Aztec's note/nullifier/commitment SETTLEMENT topology and key hierarchy; constrain the privacy claim to 'hide witnesses/keys/owners, not arbitrary computation'; treat byte-exact nullifier canonicalization across Rust/TS/Scala as a first-class requirement (same discipline as signing).

protocols.protocol: Aleo (Leo language, snarkVM/AVM, Varuna proving). Privacy-focused L1 blockchain implementing Decentralized Private Computation (DPC), descended from the ZEXE paper. Mainnet live since 2024-09-18; consensus is AleoBFT (a16z-assisted) with Proof-of-Succinct-Work puzzles. Programs written in Leo compile to Aleo instructions -> R1CS circuits proven by Varuna (a batched Marlin variant). ~350+ apps deployed at mainnet launch.
protocols.proofSystem: Varuna: a preprocessing zkSNARK in the AHP (Algebraic Holographic Proof) framework, an optimized/batched iteration of Marlin. Reduces program execution to R1CS, proven via univariate sum-check; verification key is Sonic-style KZG polynomial commitments to the indexed circuit polynomials. Batching amortizes proving cost across many function calls in one transaction (positioned for zk-rollup / proving-as-a-service). This is a GENERAL-PURPOSE SNARK over arbitrary R1CS — fundamentally different in kind from Schnorr/Sigma-protocol proofs of discrete-log relations.
protocols.trustSetup: YES — requires a trusted setup, but a UNIVERSAL and UPDATABLE one (not per-circuit). Marlin/Varuna use KZG polynomial commitments, which need a powers-of-tau Structured Reference String (SRS) generated once, circuit-independent, via a multi-party ceremony secure as long as >=1 participant per update is honest. Updatable: each contribution strengthens trust. Contrast: Schnorr/Sigma-protocols need NO trusted setup and NO SRS — only a hash (Fiat-Shamir) and public group parameters.
protocols.stateModel: Private state lives in RECORDS: UTXO-like ciphertexts stored on-chain, each with a mandatory `owner` (address authorized to spend), arbitrary data fields (app payload), and a `nonce` derived from owner's secret. Records are encrypted to the owner; only the owner can decrypt/spend. State advances by CONSUMING old records and CREATING new ones (linear/UTXO semantics). Public state lives separately in on-chain `mappings` (key-value), updated by `finalize` functions. So Aleo has a dual state model: private records (off-chain, encrypted) + public mappings (on-chain, plaintext, deterministic).
protocols.offchainOnchainSplit: Off-chain: user runs the `transition` (private function) locally in snarkVM, consuming/creating records and producing a Varuna proof of correct execution. On-chain settlement transaction carries only: (1) SERIAL NUMBERS / nullifiers of consumed records (deterministically derived from owner secret + record nonce; network rejects duplicates to prevent double-spend), (2) COMMITMENTS (hashes) of newly created records, and (3) the succinct ZK PROOF attesting all program rules were respected. No private data or addresses are revealed. The optional `finalize` portion runs publicly/on-chain (re-executed by validators, NOT zk-proven) to update mappings — purely private transfers skip finalize entirely; cross-privacy (private<->public) transitions invoke it.
protocols.assetPrivacy: Asset privacy via encrypted records: amounts, owners, and asset types are hidden inside ciphertext records. A transfer reveals only serial numbers + new commitments + proof, so amounts and sender/receiver identities stay private (shielded, Zcash-like but generalized to arbitrary program state, not just a fixed coin). Supports private, public, and mixed (private-to-public / public-to-private) value flows; the public leg uses transparent mappings.
protocols.programmability: general-purpose (arbitrary R1CS / Leo programs; private transitions + public finalize)
protocols.maturity: production (mainnet since 2024-09-18, 350+ apps, audited, public specs)
protocols.relevance: HIGH as a contrast/aspiration reference, but architecturally divergent from OttoChain. OttoChain's JLVM evaluates JSON-Logic deterministically and byte-for-byte across Rust/TS/Scala, with Schnorr/Sigma-protocol opcodes (ProveDlog/ProveDHTuple/AND-OR Fiat-Shamir trees) — NOT a general SNARK over R1CS. The two systems agree on the GOAL (off-chain execution settling on-chain with cryptographic, not economic, security) but differ on the engine: Aleo proves arbitrary computation succinctly (needs universal trusted setup + heavy proving); Sigma-protocols prove only DISCRETE-LOG-style statements (knowledge of secrets, threshold/multi-sig authorization, equality of DLs) with NO trusted setup and cheap verification. Borrowable patterns are those whose 'private' part reduces to ownership/authorization predicates rather than arbitrary hidden computation.
patternsToBorrow: Records-as-encrypted-UTXOs: model private off-chain fiber state as owner-bound commitments posted on-chain, while keeping the payload off-chain — the COMMITMENT and the consume/create lifecycle are crypto-agnostic and work with only hashes (already in JLVM via canonical JCS+hash).

Serial-number / nullifier double-spend prevention: derive a deterministic, unlinkable nullifier from owner secret + record nonce so the chain rejects replays WITHOUT learning the record — a nullifier proven via a Sigma ProveDlog (knowledge of the secret key behind a published nullifier/commitment) is fully expressible with only Sigma opcodes, no SNARK.

Transition/finalize split: cleanly separate the PRIVATE off-chain part (Sigma-proven authorization) from a PUBLIC on-chain state-machine step (the JLVM guard/effect re-evaluated deterministically by validators) — maps directly onto OttoChain's state-machine fibers + script fibers.

Ownership/authorization proofs: 'I am authorized to advance this fiber' = ProveDlog over the owner key; threshold/committee approval = AND-OR Sigma proof tree — these are the exact lineage of OttoChain's sigma opcodes and need no SNARK.
Equality/relationship proofs across commitments (e.g. value conserved, same owner across two records) where the relation is a discrete-log equality -> ProveDHTuple covers it with Sigma only.

Posting only (commitments, nullifiers, proof, transcript) on-chain to minimize on-chain footprint and reveal nothing about state — a deployment/settlement convention OttoChain can adopt regardless of proof system.
pitfalls: General-purpose hidden computation is NOT borrowable with Sigma-protocols alone. Anything where the PRIVATE part is arbitrary arithmetic over hidden inputs (private balances with hidden arithmetic conservation, range proofs on hidden amounts, hidden-input guard evaluation, confidential order matching) requires a SNARK/Bulletproof — OttoChain's JLVM+Sigma cannot prove 'this hidden JSON-Logic guard evaluated to true over secret inputs'.
Range proofs (amount in [0, 2^n)) are needed for confidential amounts; classic Sigma alone does not give them — you'd need Bulletproofs or a SNARK. Aleo gets these for free inside R1CS.

Hiding the PROGRAM/state-transition logic itself (zero-knowledge of which branch executed) needs a SNARK. With Sigma opcodes the JLVM transition is public/deterministic; only authorization secrets can be hidden, not the computation.

Universal trusted setup is a liability OttoChain avoids — but the flip side is OttoChain cannot match Varuna's 'prove arbitrary R1CS' generality. Do not promise Aleo-equivalent private programmability on a Sigma-only base.

Encrypted-record confidentiality requires an encryption-to-owner scheme + key management; the byte-for-byte JLVM canonicalization (JCS/dropNulls) must extend cleanly to whatever is hashed/committed, or commitments won't match across Rust/TS/Scala (same InvalidSignature-class failure mode the SDK already guards against).

Aleo re-executes finalize on every validator (public state is NOT private); copying the transition/finalize split means the public leg gives no privacy — set expectations that only the record/authorization layer is shielded.

snarkVM proving is GPU-heavy and latency-prone; Sigma verification is cheap, so OttoChain's advantage is cost/simplicity, not feature-parity. Frame 'privately managed off-chain fibers' as authorization-private + commitment-based, not computation-private, unless a SNARK is added later.
protocols.family: Privacy-preserving zk-blockchain / Decentralized Private Computation (ZEXE lineage). General zkSNARK over R1CS (Varuna/Marlin), encrypted UTXO records + public mappings.

protocols.protocol: Ergo Sigma Protocols + ZeroJoin/ErgoMix (Σ-protocol privacy lineage; Zerocoin->ZeroJoin)
protocols.family: Schnorr / Ergo Σ-protocol (ProveDlog + ProveDHTuple, CDS AND/OR/THRESHOLD trees, Fiat-Shamir). NOT a monolithic SNARK. ZeroJoin = Zerocoin-style ZK mixing built ENTIRELY from these Σ-leaves (specifically ProveDHTuple), no SNARK.
protocols.proofSystem: Classical interactive Σ-protocols made non-interactive by the Fiat-Shamir transform. Two atomic leaves over a prime-order group (Ergo uses secp256k1; metakit uses BN254 G1): (1) ProveDlog = Schnorr proof of knowledge of x s.t. pk=x*G; (2) ProveDHTuple = proof of knowledge of w s.t. u=g^w AND v=h^w (a DDH/Diffie-Hellman tuple). Leaves compose into AND/OR/THRESHOLD(k,n) "sigma proposition" trees via the CDS (Cramer-Damgard-Schoenmakers) challenge-splitting technique: OR = XOR of challenges, THRESHOLD = Shamir secret-sharing of the parent challenge over a small field (Ergo GF(2^192); metakit GF(2^8) byte-wise over 31-byte challenges). The root challenge is a Fiat-Shamir hash binding the full statement + all commitments + message (strong FS). Soundness rests on DLOG/DDH hardness in the random-oracle model. Linear proof size in tree size; verification is a handful of EC scalar-mults per leaf.
protocols.trustSetup: NONE. Σ-protocols need no trusted setup, no CRS, no structured reference string, no toxic waste, no powers-of-tau ceremony. Security is plain DLOG (ProveDlog) and DDH (ProveDHTuple/ZeroJoin) in the random-oracle model. This is the single biggest practical advantage over Groth16/PLONK-class SNARKs and the reason it suits a multi-language, byte-for-byte-replicated VM. (Contrast: metakit ALSO ships groth16_verify, which DOES require a per-circuit trusted setup.)
protocols.stateModel: Ergo: UTXO ("box") model. A box carries a guarding ErgoScript proposition that reduces to a SigmaBoolean (sigma proposition tree); to spend, the spender supplies a Fiat-Shamir proof satisfying that tree. There is NO general private-state register: the "state" is the box's value + protected data registers, and what is hidden is only WHICH secret/branch authorized the spend (ownership/branch privacy), not arbitrary state contents. ZeroJoin concretely: state = a pool of on-chain "mix boxes" of two kinds. (a) Half-mix box: Alice picks secret x, publishes u=g^x. (b) Full-mix boxes: Bob joins by spending Alice's half-mix box + his own equal-value box, picks (y, bit b), publishes h=g^y and v=u^y, and emits TWO indistinguishable full-mix boxes each guarded by `proveDHTuple(g,h,u,v) OR proveDlog(h)`. Alice can later spend exactly one (she knows x, so the DH-tuple (g,g^y,g^x,g^xy) holds for her box); Bob spends the other via proveDlog(y). Under DDH an observer cannot tell which output is whose. State is on-chain UTXO; the only "off-chain" part is each party's local secret (x or y).
protocols.offchainOnchainSplit: ZeroJoin deliberately moves the interaction ON-chain: it is a "non-interactive CoinJoin" where the off-chain peer coordination of CoinJoin is replaced by a public chain transaction (the full-mix tx). Off-chain = each participant's secret scalar and their choice of when to join; on-chain = the half-mix/full-mix boxes, the spend proofs (Fiat-Shamir transcripts), and the value flow. Double-spend protection is the native UTXO consumption rule (a mix box, once spent, is gone) -- there is NO separate nullifier set as in Zerocoin/Zcash, because spending the box IS the nullification and the box never re-enters a monotonic pool. Anonymity set grows with the NUMBER OF ROUNDS a coin passes through (each round halves an observer's linking probability -> 1/2^n after n rounds), NOT with a single pool's size; and the half-mix pool size is bounded by unspent half-mix boxes (deposits MINUS withdrawals), so it does NOT grow monotonically the way Zerocoin's commitment+serial pools do.
protocols.assetPrivacy: Mechanism = output indistinguishability under DDH, i.e. UNLINKABILITY of equal-denomination coins (a mixer/ring-membership privacy), NOT confidential amounts. All mix boxes must share a fixed denomination (like Zerocoin/Zcash sprout), because Σ-protocols give no native range proof / Pedersen-commitment hiding of amounts. So: sender-receiver unlinkability YES; hidden amounts NO; hidden token type NO (mixing is per-asset, per-denomination). ErgoMixer (the production product) layers Covert and Stealth addresses on top for recipient privacy. Privacy is statistical and depends on co-mixers + rounds, not cryptographically perfect like a SNARK shielded pool.
protocols.programmability: LIMITED to what is expressible as a sigma proposition (a monotone AND/OR/THRESHOLD tree of DLOG/DDH knowledge claims) optionally combined with PUBLIC predicates (height/value/data the script evaluates in the clear). Σ-protocols can prove: key ownership, ring membership (1-of-n), k-of-n thresholds, DH-tuple equality (the ZeroJoin trick), and time-locked/branching authorization. They CANNOT, on their own, express arbitrary private state transitions, hidden-input computation, range/inequality proofs over secret values, set non-membership, or anything needing a circuit -- those need a general SNARK/STARK. ErgoScript runs the surrounding logic in the CLEAR; only the authorization leaves are zero-knowledge. So you can build a state machine whose GUARDS are "prove you own/are-one-of/k-of-n", but not a state machine whose STATE is secret.
protocols.maturity: Production. Ergo sigma protocols are core consensus (live on Ergo mainnet since 2019, sigmastate-interpreter). ZeroJoin published at CBT/ESORICS 2020 (IACR ePrint 2020/560). ErgoMixer is a deployed, non-custodial mainnet mixer (>=v3.0.0 with Tor support, Covert/Stealth addresses), the canonical real-world Σ-protocol privacy product. Mature, audited, battle-tested crypto -- the Σ-leaves themselves are textbook. (metakit's port is NOT yet externally audited on its CDS/strong-FS surface -- see CryptoOps.scala maturity note -- so the design pattern is proven but OttoChain's specific implementation needs its own audit before a real spend path.)
protocols.relevance: VERY HIGH -- the most architecturally aligned protocol in the research set. metakit's JLVM is adding EXACTLY this lineage: CryptoOps.scala already implements prove_dlog_verify (Schnorr leaf), prove_dhtuple_verify (the literal ZeroJoin DDH leaf), and sigma_verify (recursive CDS AND/OR/THRESHOLD trees with strong Fiat-Shamir, 31-byte injective-into-Fr challenges, no trusted setup) over BN254 G1, with byte-for-byte Rust/TS/Scala conformance vectors. This is the same "VM runs in the clear, Σ-proofs are pure verify-precompiles" model as ErgoScript (clear logic + SigmaBoolean authorization leaves). So OttoChain can borrow the Ergo/ZeroJoin AUTHORIZATION-privacy patterns directly with the opcodes it is building, with NO new crypto: ownership proofs, ring/1-of-n membership, k-of-n thresholds, and the ZeroJoin half-mix/full-mix DH-tuple mixer as a script fiber or state-machine guard. The CRUCIAL boundary for the "privately managed off-chain fibers" design: Σ-protocols give BRANCH/OWNERSHIP privacy and unlinkable equal-denomination mixing, but they DO NOT give private off-chain STATE -- an off-chain fiber whose internal state is secret and which settles a verified-but-hidden state transition on-chain CANNOT be built from Σ-opcodes alone; that needs a general SNARK/STARK (which metakit only partially has via groth16_verify, and which carries a per-circuit trusted setup OttoChain otherwise avoids).
patternsToBorrow: Ownership / key-possession guards on fiber transitions via prove_dlog_verify (already in metakit CryptoOps.scala) -- a state-machine guard that proves the actor holds a key without a plaintext signature field.

Ring-membership (1-of-n) and k-of-n threshold authorization via sigma_verify CDS OR/THRESHOLD trees -- e.g. corporate/governance fibers where 'one of the board' or 'k-of-n directors' authorizes a transition while HIDING which member acted. This is borrowable today with only Σ-opcodes.

The ZeroJoin half-mix/full-mix unlinkable mixer, implemented as a script fiber: two equal-value outputs each guarded by `prove_dhtuple_verify(g,h,u,v) OR prove_dlog_verify(h)`, settling on-chain via normal UTXO/state consumption (no nullifier set needed). Gives per-asset, per-denomination payment unlinkability.

Strong Fiat-Shamir transcript discipline (bind full statement + all commitments + message; metakit's DomainSep + serializeTree) -- directly reusable as the canonical-signing pattern, and consistent with OttoChain's JCS(dropNulls()) determinism requirement.

Round-based privacy accounting (anonymity grows as 1/2^rounds, pool is non-monotonic) as the privacy model for any OttoChain mixing fiber -- avoids Zerocoin's ever-growing accumulator and fits a metagraph snapshot/UTXO state.

Branch-hiding authorization generally: model an off-chain fiber's DECISION/AUTHORIZATION as a sigma proposition while keeping the fiber's PUBLIC effects on-chain -- privacy of 'who/which branch', cheaply, with audited textbook crypto.
pitfalls: Σ-protocols hide WHICH secret/branch authorized a spend, NOT arbitrary state. A 'private off-chain fiber' whose internal STATE/inputs are secret and which settles a hidden state transition CANNOT be built from prove_dlog/prove_dhtuple/sigma_verify alone -- that is a SNARK/STARK requirement (general circuit), which Σ-opcodes do not provide.

No native confidential amounts or range proofs. ZeroJoin-style mixing requires FIXED denominations; you cannot hide or range-bound a secret value (balances, bids, limits) with Σ-opcodes -- needs Bulletproofs/SNARK range proofs OttoChain doesn't have.

Composing standalone prove_dlog_verify/prove_dhtuple_verify with JLVM `or`/`some` is CRYPTOGRAPHICALLY UNSOUND for OR/threshold (no challenge-splitting => no branch hiding). The ONLY sound OR/threshold is the recursive sigma_verify CDS tree. This is called out explicitly in CryptoOps.scala and is an easy, fatal mistake to make at the JSON-Logic layer.

Strong Fiat-Shamir is load-bearing: a weak transcript that omits any statement point or commitment is forgeable (SPL ZK-ElGamal / Trail-of-Bits weak-FS class). Any OttoChain Σ usage must bind the FULL statement+commitments+message under a frozen canonical byte layout, and must agree byte-for-byte across Scala/Rust/TS.

metakit's Σ surface is REGISTERED-AND-LIVE but NOT yet externally audited on its CDS/strong-FS code; conformance vectors are necessary-but-not-sufficient. Do not put it on a real mint/spend path (asset morphisms) before that audit.

Privacy is statistical, not absolute: small co-mix sets, denomination fingerprints, fee-handling leaks, and timing/amount side-channels degrade unlinkability. ZeroJoin/ErgoMix needed a NOVEL fee scheme precisely because naive fee payment de-anonymizes the mix -- any OttoChain mixing fiber must solve the same fee-privacy problem.

BN254 (metakit's curve) is ~100-bit security and has known pairing-related weakening; it's fine for these discrete-log Σ-proofs but is a weaker curve than Ergo's secp256k1 -- worth noting if Σ-proofs gate high-value asset policies.

Anonymity needs MULTIPLE rounds (1/2^n); a single mix gives only 1-of-2. Users/fibers that mix once gain little privacy -- the model must drive repeated rounds, which has UX and on-chain-cost implications.
