protocols.protocol: Zcash Sapling/Orchard + MASP (Namada) + Penumbra — the asset-privacy / shielded-pool reference layer (note commitments + nullifiers + shielded pools; Orchard Halo2 no-trusted-setup; Namada multi-asset shielded pool; Penumbra shielded swaps + flow encryption).
protocols.proofSystem:
Heterogeneous across the family, and this is the single most important distinction for OttoChain:

- Zcash Sapling: Groth16 (pairing-based zk-SNARK) over BLS12-381 with the Jubjub inner curve. Requires a circuit-specific trusted setup (the "Sapling MPC ceremony" / powers-of-tau). Sprout used Groth16's predecessor (BCTV14/PGHR13) with a per-circuit toxic-waste ceremony.
- Zcash Orchard: Halo2 — a PLONKish IOP with an inner-product (Bulletproofs-style) polynomial commitment, instantiated on the Pallas/Vesta ("Pasta") amicable curve cycle. NO trusted setup (no toxic waste); the cycle enables (future) recursion. This is the only member of the family with a transparent setup. Nullifier: nf = Extract_P([(F_nk(rho) + psi) mod p]·G + cm).
- Namada MASP: Sapling-derived Groth16 over BLS12-381/Jubjub. REQUIRES a trusted setup — and notably the Zcash Sapling parameters cannot be fully reused, so MASP ran its own MPC ceremony. Adds a third "Convert" circuit alongside the Sapling Spend/Output circuits.
- Penumbra: Groth16 over BLS12-377 (chosen over BLS12-381 to allow depth-1 recursion later) with the decaf377 prime-order group as the in-circuit inner group. REQUIRES a trusted setup (decentralized Groth16 ceremony, one proving/verifying key per fixed action statement). The common belief that Penumbra is Halo2 is WRONG — it is fixed-statement Groth16.

Bottom line: every member uses a GENERAL-PURPOSE zk-SNARK/zk-IOP to prove the private state-transition relation in zero knowledge. Three of four need a trusted setup; only Orchard (Halo2) is setup-free. NONE is a Σ-protocol system. Penumbra additionally uses a SEPARATE, non-SNARK primitive — additively-homomorphic threshold encryption (flow encryption) — which is the one component conceptually reachable with Schnorr/Σ-style crypto.
protocols.trustSetup: Required for Sapling (Groth16 MPC), Namada MASP (its own Groth16 MPC, cannot reuse Sapling params), and Penumbra (Groth16 decentralized ceremony, per-statement keys). NOT required for Orchard (Halo2 transparent setup — this is the headline reason Zcash moved Sprout→Sapling→Orchard, eliminating toxic waste). For OttoChain: Σ-protocols (Schnorr/ProveDlog/ProveDHTuple/AND-OR Fiat-Shamir) are themselves transparent (no trusted setup), matching Orchard's trust profile but NOT its expressive power.
protocols.stateModel:
Shielded-pool UTXO model, uniform across all four:
- Private state = a set of NOTES. A note binds (recipient address / diversified pkd, value v, asset type, randomness rho/psi/rcm). In MASP each note also carries an explicit asset identifier; in Sapling/Orchard the asset is implicitly ZEC.
- On-chain, each created note appears only as a hiding-binding NOTE COMMITMENT (cm), appended as a leaf to an append-only incremental Merkle tree (Sapling note-commitment tree; Penumbra calls it the State Commitment Tree / Tiered Commitment Tree). The chain stores commitments, never plaintext notes.
- Spending a note publishes a NULLIFIER — a deterministic, unlinkable tag derived from the note plus the owner's nullifier key. The chain keeps a nullifier set; a nullifier may appear at most once. This is the double-spend / replay guard, decoupled from which commitment is being spent (spend-unlinkability).
- A spend proves in zero knowledge: "I know an opening of some commitment in the tree (Merkle-membership) whose nullifier is X, and I own it." The Merkle root is the only public anchor.
- VALUE COMMITMENTS (Pedersen, homomorphic) per spend/output let the verifier check balance by summing commitments to zero WITHOUT learning amounts. MASP's Convert circuit extends this: it injects "convert" value commitments so the homomorphic sum of Spend+Output+Convert is zero, enabling shielded burn/mint between asset types at a public ratio. Penumbra reuses the same homomorphic value-commitment trick for batched DEX flows.
protocols.offchainOnchainSplit:
Wallet/client-side (off-chain) vs chain (on-chain) is sharp and consistent — and is the most directly studyable pattern for OttoChain's "private off-chain fiber settling on-chain":
- OFF-CHAIN (prover/wallet): holds note plaintexts, scans the chain with viewing keys to detect incoming notes (trial-decryption of note ciphertexts), builds the spend, computes nullifiers, and generates the zk proof of the state transition. All "execution" (deciding what notes to spend/create) happens client-side.
- ON-CHAIN (verifier/consensus): receives only (nullifiers, new commitments, value-commitment balance check, zk-proof, Merkle anchor). It verifies the proof against the published anchor, checks nullifier-nonmembership, appends new commitments, and records nullifiers. The chain re-executes NOTHING private — it only verifies a succinct transcript.
- Penumbra adds a second settlement style for the DEX: per-block BATCH settlement. Individual encrypted swap intents are aggregated; only the NET cross-pair flow is decrypted and settled on-chain at end of block (sealed-bid batch auction, frontrun-resistant). This is "many private off-chain intents → one public on-chain settlement," the closest analogue to private off-chain fibers batching into an on-chain commit.
The general shape "private execution off-chain, publish {nullifiers, commitments, proof/transcript}, chain verifies + advances an accumulator" is exactly the template a private off-chain fiber would follow.
protocols.assetPrivacy:
- Sapling/Orchard: single-asset (ZEC). Amounts hidden via Pedersen value commitments; sender/receiver hidden via diversified addresses + encrypted note ciphertexts; linkage hidden via nullifiers. One unified anonymity set.
- MASP (Namada): MULTI-ASSET shielded pool — the reference design. Every asset gets a deterministic "asset type" (a hash-to-curve generator); value commitments are per-asset-type Pedersen commitments so the homomorphic balance check is per asset. The Convert circuit allows shielded asset conversion (e.g. rewards/inflation, or pegged conversions) at a public ratio without unshielding. Crucially, ALL assets share ONE anonymity set, so the privacy of each asset grows with total pool activity.
- Penumbra: also a multi-asset shielded pool (Sapling-derived) plus FLOW ENCRYPTION for the DEX/governance: amounts are additively-homomorphic threshold-encrypted, validators sum ciphertexts and threshold-decrypt only the aggregate (net swap flow / vote tally), so individual amounts stay private even at settlement. Liquidity positions are created anonymously.
protocols.programmability: Deliberately LIMITED — none is a general programmable state machine. All four expose a FIXED menu of action/circuit types (spend, output, and for MASP convert; for Penumbra additionally delegate/undelegate, swap/swap-claim, position-open/close, governance vote, IBC). Each action type is its own hand-written circuit with (except Orchard) its own proving/verifying key. There is no user-deployable contract, no Turing-complete shielded VM, no arbitrary private state machine. Adding new private functionality = writing and (re-)ceremonying a new circuit. Penumbra explicitly justifies Groth16 by 'an initial set of FIXED functionality.' So: rich asset privacy, essentially zero general programmability inside the shielded domain. (Namada offers limited programmability only by UNSHIELDING to interact with transparent apps — i.e. leaving privacy.)
protocols.maturity:
Production / battle-tested at the cryptographic layer.
- Zcash Sapling: live since 2018; Orchard activated with NU5 (May 2022); both in continuous mainnet use, heavily audited, formally specified (Zcash Protocol Spec, ZIP-224/225/226).
- Namada MASP: mainnet launched late 2024; MASP audited; ran its own trusted-setup ceremony; shielded-pool incentives live.
- Penumbra: mainnet launched 2024; circuits independently audited (zkSecurity). Note: flow-encryption for the DEX is partially future work in the spec (initial DEX reveals batched amounts; full per-swap flow-encryption is a planned upgrade) — so treat Penumbra's flow-encryption as design-mature but partially aspirational, while its shielded pool + batch auction are live.
protocols.relevance:
HIGH as a reference architecture for "private off-chain fibers settling on-chain," but with a HARD CRYPTO CEILING for OttoChain's Σ-protocol-only (Schnorr/ProveDlog/ProveDHTuple/AND-OR, no SNARK) JLVM.

What maps cleanly onto Σ-protocols + JLVM (BORROWABLE NOW):
1. The settlement TEMPLATE: execute privately off-chain, then publish {nullifier(s), new state commitment(s), a verifiable transcript}; the chain verifies a transcript + advances an append-only accumulator and a spent-set. JLVM guards/effects can enforce 'nullifier not in set', 'append commitment', 'verify proof transcript' as ordinary state-machine transitions. This is settlement plumbing, not ZK, and needs no SNARK.
2. COMMITMENT + NULLIFIER accounting as a Σ-protocol pattern: a Pedersen/commitment opening proven with a Schnorr/ProveDlog Σ-proof, and a nullifier as a deterministic DH-tuple tag (ProveDHTuple: nf relates a secret key and a note tag by a common discrete log) proven equal-without-revealing via the classic Chaum-Pedersen DH-tuple Σ-protocol. Double-spend prevention via a public nullifier set is pure bookkeeping. So 'unlinkable one-time spend tags with ownership proof' IS expressible with ProveDHTuple — genuinely borrowable.
3. AND-OR proof trees (Σ-protocol composition, exactly the Ergo lineage you're adding): ring/threshold/policy authorization over notes — 'spendable by key A AND (B OR C)' — proven without revealing which branch. Directly borrowable; this is what Σ-protocols are best at.
4. Penumbra FLOW ENCRYPTION / batch-aggregation: additively-homomorphic (ElGamal-style on a Schnorr-friendly group) threshold encryption + DKG is Σ-protocol-adjacent (threshold Schnorr / Pedersen DKG + Chaum-Pedersen decryption proofs). 'Many private off-chain intents → aggregate → reveal only the net on-chain' is achievable WITHOUT a SNARK, and is the single most relevant borrowable pattern for private-off-chain-fiber batching/settlement on OttoChain.
5. Homomorphic VALUE-COMMITMENT balance check (sum-to-zero of Pedersen commitments) needs no SNARK by itself — only range proofs do.

What REQUIRES a general SNARK and is therefore OUT OF REACH with Σ-protocols alone:
A. ZERO-KNOWLEDGE MERKLE MEMBERSHIP: proving a spent commitment is some leaf in a large tree WITHOUT revealing which leaf. This is the heart of shielded-pool anonymity and needs a circuit (SNARK/Bulletproofs/STARK). Σ-protocols give you a proof about a KNOWN public commitment, not hidden-index membership over a large set. Without it you get 'verifiable private state + unlinkable nullifiers' but NOT a large shared anonymity set — anonymity collapses toward the size of a small explicit OR-ring (Σ-protocol ring proofs scale linearly, so only tiny rings are practical).
B. RANGE PROOFS / hidden-amount arithmetic at scale: proving 0 <= v < 2^64 and balance constraints with hidden values needs Bulletproofs or a SNARK; naive Σ-protocol range proofs are too large. So fully-hidden multi-asset amounts (MASP-grade) are not free.
C. The MASP CONVERT circuit and any general private STATE-MACHINE transition (arbitrary guard/effect evaluated in zero knowledge) are SNARK-shaped. JLVM can evaluate guards/effects in the CLEAR (byte-for-byte Rust/TS/Scala) and prove signatures/openings with Σ-protocols, but it CANNOT prove 'this JSON-Logic transition was applied correctly to HIDDEN inputs' without a circuit for the JLVM itself.

PRACTICAL TAKEAWAY for OttoChain: With only Σ-protocols, target a 'verifiable/authorized private off-chain fiber' model — private off-chain state whose AUTHORIZATION, ownership, one-time-spend tags (nullifiers via ProveDHTuple), policy logic (AND-OR trees), and batched/threshold settlement (flow-encryption-style) are Σ-proven and JLVM-checked — rather than a 'fully shielded anonymity-set' model. You get unlinkable spends, hidden policy branches, threshold-aggregated private settlement, and commit/nullifier bookkeeping; you do NOT get a large hidden anonymity set or hidden-amount/hidden-transition proofs (those are the SNARK-only part). Penumbra's batch-flow settlement and the Chaum-Pedersen/DH-tuple nullifier construction are the highest-value borrowable ideas; the shielded Merkle-membership core is the part to consciously drop or replace with explicit small-ring or transparent designs.
patternsToBorrow: Off-chain-execute / on-chain-verify settlement template: chain consumes only {nullifiers, new commitments, transcript, accumulator anchor} and advances an append-only commitment tree + a spent/nullifier set — expressible directly as JLVM guards/effects, no SNARK needed.

Nullifiers as deterministic, unlinkable one-time spend tags derived from (note, owner nullifier key), with a public nullifier set for double-spend/replay prevention — realizable as a Chaum-Pedersen DH-tuple Σ-proof (your ProveDHTuple opcode) instead of a circuit.

Hiding-binding note commitments + Pedersen value commitments with HOMOMORPHIC sum-to-zero balance checking (MASP per-asset-type generators for multi-asset) — the balance check needs no SNARK; only range-bounding amounts does.

AND-OR Σ-protocol proof trees (the Ergo/Sigma lineage you are adding) for note spend policies / ring/threshold authorization, proving WHICH branch without revealing it — natively Σ-protocol, directly borrowable.

Penumbra flow encryption / batch settlement: additively-homomorphic threshold encryption + validator DKG so many private off-chain intents aggregate into a single public on-chain net settlement — buildable with threshold-Schnorr / Pedersen DKG + Chaum-Pedersen decryption proofs, NO SNARK; the strongest analogue to private-off-chain-fiber batching.
Append-only incremental Merkle commitment tree with a published root as the sole public state anchor — a transparent accumulator pattern reusable as ordinary JLVM state even without ZK membership.

Viewing-key / trial-decryption note discovery: clients scan the chain and detect their own private state off-chain via encrypted note ciphertexts — an off-chain indexing pattern independent of the proof system.

Orchard's transparent (no-trusted-setup) posture as the design target: Σ-protocols are likewise setup-free, so match Orchard's trust model even though you cannot match its anonymity-set expressiveness.
pitfalls: DO NOT assume Penumbra is Halo2 — it is fixed-statement Groth16 over BLS12-377 (decaf377) and REQUIRES a trusted setup. Only Orchard is Halo2 / setup-free. Conflating them mis-states the trust model.

The large shielded ANONYMITY SET depends on zero-knowledge Merkle MEMBERSHIP (proving a spend is SOME leaf without revealing which). Σ-protocols cannot do this at scale — ring proofs are linear-size, so practical rings are tiny. Without a SNARK you get unlinkable spends but only a small/explicit anonymity set, not Zcash-grade privacy. Be explicit that this is dropped.

Fully HIDDEN AMOUNTS at scale need range proofs (Bulletproofs/SNARK). The homomorphic sum-to-zero check is cheap, but bounding each value to prevent overflow/negative-value forgery is NOT free with plain Σ-protocols.

MASP's CONVERT circuit and ANY private state-MACHINE transition over HIDDEN inputs are SNARK-shaped. JLVM evaluating JSON-Logic in the CLEAR + Σ-proofs of signatures/openings does NOT prove a hidden-input transition was computed correctly — there is no circuit for the JLVM itself.

Trusted-setup ceremonies are a liability and an operational burden (MASP couldn't even reuse Zcash's params). Choosing Σ-protocols sidesteps this, but don't claim feature parity with shielded pools that bought their privacy with that ceremony.

Flow-encryption / threshold-decryption introduces a LIVENESS + COLLUSION trust assumption on the validator/decryptor set (threshold honesty, DKG correctness, epoch key rotation). It is not unconditional privacy and is partly future-work even in Penumbra's own spec — don't overstate its maturity.

Nullifier-set and commitment-tree growth are unbounded append-only state; production systems need careful note-management, tree epoching, and scanning performance — a real engineering cost the JLVM/fiber settlement layer would inherit.

Canonicalization caveat for OttoChain specifically: any Σ-proof transcript or commitment serialized into a fiber payload must round-trip through JCS(dropNulls(...)) byte-for-byte across Rust/TS/Scala, or Fiat-Shamir challenges/signatures diverge and yield opaque InvalidSignature — the same parity discipline already required for canonical-z/low31 sigma opcodes.

protocols.protocol: Client-side / overlay proving family — primary: Mina zkApps (off-chain state + on-chain commitment, recursive zk); secondary references for contrast: RAILGUN (on-chain SNARK privacy pool) and Aztec Connect (private zk-rollup, sunset 2023). The brief names Mina as "closest to bolting privacy onto an existing metagraph without rebuilding the L1," so this object centers Mina and uses Railgun/Aztec as comparison points.
protocols.family: Client-side / overlay proving — privacy as an overlay computed in the user's client (browser/wallet), settled on a base chain via an on-chain verifier, rather than baked into L1 consensus.
protocols.proofSystem: MINA (most relevant): Kimchi (a PLONK variant) wrapped by the Pickles recursion layer. Kimchi replaces PLONK's pairing/KZG polynomial commitment with an inner-product argument (IPA, Bulletproofs-style), so it is TRANSPARENT — no per-circuit trusted setup / no toxic waste. Security rests on discrete-log hardness over the Pasta cycle of curves (Pallas/Vesta) plus Fiat-Shamir for non-interactivity. The Pasta 2-cycle is what makes cheap recursion ("proofs of proofs") possible: prove on one curve, verify on the other without field emulation. This is a GENERAL-PURPOSE SNARK over arithmetic circuits — strictly more expressive than a Σ-protocol. RAILGUN: Groth16 zk-SNARK, per-circuit trusted setup via Perpetual Powers of Tau (1-honest-party assumption). AZTEC CONNECT: PLONK zk-SNARK (in-house, universal/updatable setup via a large MPC ceremony). Note: Mina/Kimchi being transparent + DLog-based is the one in the same cryptographic neighborhood as OttoChain's Σ-protocol opcodes (both Schnorr/Fiat-Shamir over EC groups), but Kimchi is a full circuit prover, not a bare Σ-protocol.
protocols.stateModel: MINA: Two-layer. (1) On-chain: each zkApp account has exactly 8 field-element slots of on-chain storage. Larger state lives off-chain as a single Merkle Map (Merkle tree of fields / key-value entries); only its Merkle root (a commitment, held in an OffchainState.Commitments field) is stored on-chain. Private inputs are processed client-side and only attestations/commitments reach the chain — raw data never leaves the user's machine. (2) Concurrency is handled by an Actions + Reducer dispatch model: txns dispatch "actions" (queued state-change intents) against a precondition; a later settle() consumes the pending action queue via a recursive reducer (createSettlementProof) and advances the committed root. All state is recoverable from actions alone. RAILGUN / AZTEC CONNECT: UTXO "note" model — private state is a set of encrypted commitments (notes: owner pubkey, asset id, value, blinding) accumulated in an on-chain Merkle tree; spending reveals a nullifier (hash of spending key + note path) to prevent double-spends without linking to the note. Aztec adds claim notes / defi-interaction notes to bridge to public Ethereum DeFi.
protocols.offchainOnchainSplit: MINA: Execution and proving happen entirely off-chain/client-side (o1js in the browser); the chain stores only the 8 on-chain fields + the off-chain Merkle root and verifies the recursive proof. settle() maps a batch of off-chain action-driven transitions to a single on-chain commitment update — the on-chain footprint is a commitment + a succinct proof, NOT a transcript or per-step replay. RAILGUN: client builds + proves a join-split locally; on-chain the verifier checks the SNARK, inserts new commitment leaves, and records nullifiers (commitment-insert + nullifier-publish is the settlement). AZTEC CONNECT: users prove join-split/account/claim circuits client-side; a sequencer/rollup provider aggregates many user proofs into a rollup proof verified once on L1, which then maps internal asset_ids to real ETH/ERC-20 movements via the RollupProcessor. Common pattern across all three: heavy compute off-chain, on-chain you only verify a proof and mutate a small commitment/nullifier set.
protocols.assetPrivacy: MINA: Not primarily an asset-privacy protocol — it gives general programmable privacy (private inputs/state via commitments and attestations). Token amounts are not natively hidden by a shielded-pool primitive the way Railgun/Aztec do it; you'd build confidentiality yourself in-circuit. RAILGUN: dedicated shielded pool — ERC-20/NFTs are "shielded" into a 0zk address; balances, amounts, and sender/recipient links are hidden via encrypted UTXO notes + nullifiers; relayers break the gas-payer linkage; Private Proofs of Innocence for compliance. AZTEC CONNECT: shielded zk-assets with hidden sender/value, bridged to public DeFi (interaction values become public at the bridge boundary, but membership/identity stays private).
protocols.programmability: MINA: HIGH — arbitrary application logic and state machines expressible as o1js zkPrograms / smart contracts; preconditions = assertions in-circuit, account updates carry events/preconditions, recursion lifts the per-proof constraint budget so computation is effectively unbounded (at extra proving cost). Main friction is concurrency (precondition races) which forces the Actions/Reducer pattern. This is general-purpose because it is a full SNARK over circuits. RAILGUN: LOW/FIXED — a small set of fixed audited circuits (shield/unshield/transfer/join-split); not a general app platform, though it can call external DeFi contracts from the shielded balance. AZTEC CONNECT: LOW/FIXED circuits (account/join-split/claim) bridging to whitelisted external "bridge contracts"; general programmability only arrived later in the (separate) Aztec Network + Noir, after Connect was sunset.
protocols.maturity: MINA zkApps: Production L1 (mainnet, Berkeley/Kimchi upgrade live); o1js + off-chain-storage tooling are released and actively used; the recursive-proof model is battle-tested but client-side proving is heavy and concurrency patterns are still a known sharp edge. RAILGUN: Live in production on Ethereum, BSC, Polygon, Arbitrum; tens of thousands of txns and tens of millions of $ in the relay contract as of 2026 — the most production-proven asset-privacy overlay here. AZTEC CONNECT: SUNSET in 2023 (team deliberately shut it down to build the fully programmable Aztec Network + Noir); valuable as a design reference, not a live target. Its main lesson: fixed-circuit private bridges hit a programmability ceiling, motivating a general private VM.
protocols.trustSetup: MINA: NONE (transparent) — Kimchi's IPA commitment removes the trusted setup; relies on DLog + Fiat-Shamir. This is the key differentiator and the one most aligned with OttoChain's no-ceremony Σ-protocol posture. RAILGUN: Per-circuit trusted setup (Groth16) via Perpetual Powers of Tau MPC (secure if ≥1 participant deletes toxic waste). AZTEC CONNECT: Universal/updatable trusted setup (PLONK) via a large MPC ceremony.
protocols.relevance: VERY RELEVANT structurally; PARTIALLY borrowable with Σ-protocols alone. Mina zkApps is the right architectural template — off-chain client-side state machine, on-chain stores only a commitment (8 fields + off-chain Merkle root) advanced by an Actions/Reducer settle, with a TRANSPARENT no-trusted-setup proof system (Kimchi/IPA/DLog) that matches OttoChain's ceremony-free Σ-protocol posture. With only Schnorr/Σ-opcodes (ProveDlog, ProveDHTuple, AND-OR Fiat-Shamir) OttoChain CAN build a commit-and-authorize private off-chain fiber: on-chain commitment to canonical JSON state (reusing existing JCS(dropNulls) byte-for-byte parity as the determinism layer), Σ-based authorization/ownership/threshold predicates, and Railgun-style Schnorr/DH-tuple nullifiers for double-spend/replay protection. What it CANNOT do without a general (ideally transparent) SNARK: prove that a hidden JLVM transition was a VALID run of the fiber's JSON-Logic guard/effect, provide confidential amounts with range proofs, or recursively aggregate many private transitions. So the settlement + authorization + nullifier patterns are borrowable now; verifiable private computation is the hard wall and is exactly what Mina has and OttoChain does not.
patternsToBorrow: Mina-style off-chain state with on-chain commitment: store only a hash/commitment of the canonical JSON state (JCS(dropNulls(state))) on the fiber, keep plaintext client-side — leverages OttoChain's existing byte-for-byte canonicalization as the determinism layer a commitment needs.

Mina Actions+Reducer settle() pattern: dispatch transition intents against a precondition, batch-advance the committed root via a settle step — clean fit for an on-chain fiber that only mutates a commitment.

Schnorr/ProveDHTuple nullifiers (Railgun-style): deterministic key-derived tags proven via Σ-protocol to prevent double-spend/replay of private transitions WITHOUT a SNARK — highest-value borrowable primitive given metakit's new sigma opcodes.
ProveDlog / AND-OR proof trees for authorization, ownership, and threshold/multi-party access control on private transitions — maps directly to identity/governance/corporate fibers.

Transparent, no-trusted-setup posture: follow Mina/Kimchi (IPA, DLog, Fiat-Shamir) rather than Groth16/PLONK ceremonies — aligns with OttoChain's ceremony-free Σ-protocol stance and avoids toxic-waste operational risk.

Encrypted UTXO note model (Railgun/Aztec) for any asset-privacy fiber where the value relations are simple enough to be DH-tuple-expressible; defer confidential-amount arithmetic until range proofs are in scope.
Relayer/separated-gas-payer pattern (Railgun) to break the linkage between the on-chain settler and the private actor.
pitfalls: Σ-protocols CANNOT prove arbitrary JLVM execution — do not promise 'verifiable private state transitions' from sigma opcodes alone; proving a JSON-Logic guard/effect ran correctly in ZK needs a circuit/SNARK OttoChain does not have. This is the central scoping trap.

Confidential amounts need range proofs (Bulletproofs-class), not bare Schnorr — without them a hidden-value note scheme is unsound (negative/overflow values). Bulletproofs are still transparent/DLog so they're a plausible add, but they are NOT in the current sigma-opcode set.

Commitment determinism is load-bearing: any divergence between Rust/TS/Scala JCS(dropNulls) canonicalization silently breaks commitment equality (mirrors the existing InvalidSignature/opaque-400 failure mode) — the commitment hash must be computed over the SAME canonical bytes the signing path uses.

Mina's concurrency sharp edge transfers: naive precondition-on-commitment settlement causes races when multiple clients advance the same off-chain fiber; you must adopt the Actions/Reducer queue or serialize settlement.

Trusted setup is a real liability for the SNARK alternatives (Railgun Groth16 / Aztec PLONK) — if OttoChain ever reaches for general proving, prefer transparent systems (Kimchi/Halo2/Bulletproofs) to keep the no-ceremony property.

Aztec Connect's shutdown shows fixed-circuit privacy bridges hit a programmability ceiling — a Σ-only overlay is similarly bounded; be explicit that it covers commit/authorize/nullify, not general private apps, so the roadmap doesn't overcommit.

Nullifier design must bind to the canonical note + the spending key via ProveDHTuple correctly, or you get either linkability (privacy loss) or forgeable double-spends (soundness loss); this is subtle even though it's 'just' a Σ-protocol.
On-chain you settle a commitment, not a transcript — resist storing JLVM execution transcripts on-chain to 'prove' transitions; that leaks the private state and defeats the overlay.
